Subject: Solace hosted API - residency and retention follow-ups

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Contracts pinged us for a few clarifications we need to include in our security questionnaire:

1) Is customer request/feature data stored in a specific region? We need to confirm where payloads and derived artifacts (embeddings, logs) are stored for hosted customers.
2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, message payloads, embeddings, and model interaction telemetry (traces/errors)?
3) How do deletions requested by the customer propagate to backups and snapshots? Expected timelines?
4) Do you retain any data in long-term backups for disaster recovery beyond the specified retention windows? If yes, how is that data scoped?
5) If we request immediate deletion for a subset of tenants, can you provide an attestation that caches (KV cache, model prompt caches) and ephemeral artifacts are purged?

We attached the relevant questionnaire excerpt (solace_questionnaire.xlsx). Can you respond with the wording our security team can include?

Appreciate it — Ari

Hi Ari — thanks for sending the questionnaire. Below are concise answers you can paste into your security form; I’ve included practical timelines and controls. I’m copying Neha (Security) for technical fidelity and Camila (Solutions) for any architecture diagrams you want attached.

1) Region of storage
- For hosted customers without geofencing, primary customer payloads and derived artifacts are stored in the nearest Redwood-managed cloud region by default (US: us-west-2 and us-east-1). Customers can request region pinning to a single region (e.g., us-east-1) as part of onboarding.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request payloads (raw requests and immediate response tokens): 30 days by default.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: 90 days by default.
- Operational logs (API access logs, request metrics): 30 days by default; aggregated metrics retained longer in anonymized form.
- Debugging traces & error telemetry: 14 days.
- These windows can be tightened (shorter retention) via contract for enterprise customers.

3) Deletion propagation to backups and snapshots
- Primary deletion flow: when a customer uses the API/Data Deletion request, data is removed from live stores within 24 hours.
- Backups/snapshots: backups are rotated daily and retained for a rolling 7-day period. Deletion requests trigger background reconciliation to remove items from incremental backups where possible; full removal from backup snapshots completes within 30 days in standard hosted mode.
- Emergency/accelerated erasures: for enterprise contracts we offer expedited purge (target: 7 days) backed by an attestation.

4) Long-term backups for DR
- We do not keep long-term, unscoped backups containing customer request payloads beyond the 7-day snapshot retention in standard hosted plans. Disaster recovery snapshots older than 7 days are not persisted with identifiable customer request payloads. Logs used for capacity planning and anonymized metrics may be kept longer but are stripped of customer identifiers.

5) Caches and ephemeral artifacts
- KV caches and runtime model prompt caches are ephemeral and not treated as durable stores; they are evicted on-demand. An erasure request triggers cache invalidation for the affected tenant and associated keys within the live serving fleet (90th percentile: within minutes, full propagation across nodes within 24 hours).

6) Evidence & attestations
- We provide an auditable deletion job record (job id and timestamps) for each erasure request. For customers requiring stronger evidence, we can provide a signed attestation PDF and a filtered export of deletion job records. SOC 2 report access is available under NDA.

Attachments: redwood-erasure-playbook.pdf (high level process), hosted-data-flow.svg (architecture flow).

If you want, we can produce a short attestation statement we can sign and a timeline SLA to include in your contract.

Short answer you can paste: "Redwood Inference (hosted) stores customer request payloads and derived artifacts in the selected Redwood-managed cloud region (default US regions). Standard retention windows are: request payloads 30 days, embeddings 90 days, operational logs 30 days, traces 14 days. Deletion requests remove data from live stores within 24 hours and from backups within 30 days; expedited erasures can be contracted. KV and runtime caches are invalidated on erasure — propagation completed across nodes within 24 hours. Deletion activity is recorded and an attestation can be provided upon request."

Let me know if you want tighter contractual language and we’ll loop Legal.

— Mateo Alvarez

Thanks Mateo — this is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security team before we mark this closed: 

• Can you confirm whether the 30-day backup window includes immutable disaster recovery archives (i.e., do any immutable snapshots exist outside the 7-day rolling snapshot policy)?
• For the attestation language: can Neha confirm the deletion job record includes (a) job id, (b) initiating principal, (c) affected tenant id(s), (d) timestamps for live removal and backup reconciliation?
• Does the deletion workflow purge model-side caches (e.g., local KV caches on GPUs) or only service-side caches? We need to ensure model caches do not retain user prompts longer than live storage TTLs.

If we can get three bullet confirmations we can include them directly in our doc and share back to contracts.

— Ari

Hi Ari — quick confirmations below (Neha tagged for any additional notes).

• Immutable DR archives: Redwood does not maintain separate immutable archives containing identifiable customer request payloads beyond the 7-day rolling snapshot window for standard hosted customers. Disaster recovery snapshots older than 7 days are stored only in an anonymized, aggregated form that cannot be reconstituted to individual request payloads.

• Deletion job record fields: yes — each customer-initiated deletion job record includes a unique job id, initiating principal (API key or admin user), affected tenant id(s), and timestamps for live-store removal and backup reconciliation attempts. We can provide a filtered export of these fields for attestation under NDA.

• Model-side caches: runtime model KV caches and GPU-local caches are considered ephemeral. Our serving runtime actively evicts or invalidates cached keys associated with a tenant on erasure. Practical notes: active in-memory caches are invalidated within minutes; full propagation (including draining in-flight requests and restarting affected processes where necessary) completes within 24 hours. We do not persist KV cache contents to long-term storage.

Attached: redwood-erasure-attestation.pdf (signed example attestation we produce for enterprise erasure requests). If you want this exact language signed for Solace, confirm and I’ll route it through Legal (we can include a 7-day SLA for backup purge in an addendum).
